tests.question: How should the onboarding experience relate to the promises made by marketing?
tests.evidence: So I like to think of your brand is the promise that you're making and your product experience is your delivery of that promise.

answer.summary: Onboarding should help deliver the promise marketing makes, since the product experience is the delivery of the brand promise.

sections.heading: Align onboarding with the promise
sections.content: Treat onboarding as part of the product experience: it should deliver on the promise made by marketing, rather than create a gap between what was promised and what users experience.

sections.heading: Survey response choices

tests.question: What disappointment-survey percentage separated fast-growing companies from companies struggling to grow?
tests.evidence: What he found, is that the companies that struggled to grow almost always had less than 40%, very disappointed. Whereas the companies that grew the fastest almost always had more than 40%, very disappointed.

answer.summary: The dividing point was 40%: fast-growing companies generally had more than 40% of users say they would be very disappointed without the product, while struggling companies had less than 40%.

sections.heading: Disappointment-survey threshold
sections.content: Companies struggling to grow almost always had less than 40% of respondents who would be “very disappointed” without the product; the fastest-growing companies almost always had more than 40%.
